name: FIM-92 Stinger

image.license: See Commons file page for license

cost.display: ~$120–150K per missile at current production (NATO bulk-buy pricing has run far higher, ~$830K/round, reflecting scarce production capacity)

short_role: Shoulder-fired, infrared-homing short-range air defense missile — the last-ditch layer against low, fast, close-in air threats.
characteristics: One-person portable and operable, no vehicle required
Infrared seeker homes on the heat signature of an aircraft or helicopter, less effective against small cold drone airframes
Fielded in large numbers relative to its cost, giving infantry units organic short-range air defense
employment_notes: Sits at the bottom of the layered air-defense stack, covering the close-in gap between longer-range SAMs and gun-based CUAS — genuinely effective against helicopters and fixed-wing aircraft, but a poor tool against small, low-heat-signature FPV and loitering-munition drones, which is why it is paired with gun-based CUAS rather than relied on alone against the drone threat.
contrast_vs_traditional: Stinger was built for a Cold War threat picture (attack helicopters, low-flying jets) and remains genuinely effective against exactly that threat. What changed is what shares its airspace: infantry now also need organic defense against a mass of cheap drones the Stinger's infrared seeker isn't well suited to, which is why short-range air defense has diversified into a mixed missile-and-gun layer rather than staying a single-system solution.

connections.description: Receives early-warning cueing on inbound low-altitude tracks.
